title: Prompt Lint and Telemetry Presets Quickstart
content:
Purpose:
This quickstart is a compact playbook for embedding two lightweight developer-experience primitives into SDK integrations and starter apps: (1) prompt linting (fast, deterministic checks to catch common mistakes) and (2) telemetry presets (minimal, privacy-preserving signals we want collected by default). The goal: reduce first-week regressions from prompt mistakes and make telemetry signals comparable across teams.

Audience:
- SDK engineers building examples and starter apps
- Developer advocates and solutions engineers creating onramp kits
- Integrators who want low-effort observability and prompt hygiene

Goals (what success looks like):
- A 2–3 minute checklist that can be dropped into any sample app to enable prompt lint + telemetry.
- Default telemetry schema small enough to ship without asking legal for every customer.
- A terse list of prompt-lint rules that catch ~80% of early user errors (missing system prompt, bad stop sequences, too-long context, unscoped tool calls).

Non-goals:
- Full eval suite or exhaustive prompt-quality scoring.
- Deep PII extraction or data-retention policies (those live in security/compliance docs).

Quickstart overview (developer flow):
1) Add the preset dependency (pseudo):
   - npm: npm i @redwood/ux-presets (placeholder name)
   - python: pip install redwood-ux-presets
2) Wire up on SDK client init:
   - call Preset.attach(client, { env: 'sandbox', telemetryOptIn: 'default' })
3) Add lint middleware for outgoing prompts (synchronous check). If lint fails, return a helpful error in dev mode; in CI it should fail the build.
4) Start capturing telemetry using the presets (see below). Telemetry is sampled by default (1% in preview, configurable).

Minimal preset (what gets collected by default):
- session_id (uuid, ephemeral)
- sdk: {name, version}
- sample_rate: how telemetry was sampled for the request (string)
- model_hint: model name or family (not full version/hash unless permitted)
- route: logical route / sample-app-flow id
- prompt_metadata: { length_tokens: numeric, has_system_prompt: boolean, contains_functions: boolean }
- latency_ms: end-to-end duration for the API call
- outcome: generation_result (success|error|fallback)
- error_codes: list of normalized error ids (if any)

Privacy note: presets avoid capturing user text. prompt_metadata intentionally stores only counts and booleans. Any capture of user content must be explicitly enabled by customers and vetted by legal.

Prompt-lint rules (fast, pluggable checks):
- MUST include system prompt for multi-turn assistants: warn if missing and conversation looks assistant-like.
- NO raw API keys in prompt text: regex scan for patterns, fail dev-mode run.
- STOP tokens sanity: detect contradictory stop sequences or empty stops that may hang streaming clients.
- MAX_CONTEXT: warn if prompt length (tokens) > configured threshold (default 6k tokens) and suggest summarization.
- TOOL_CALL_SCOPE: if function/tool calling is enabled, confirm the function list is provided and no unknown tool references are present.
- TEMPERATURE_RANGE: warn if temperature is outside [0,2]; fail CI if >1.5 in production-sample.

Example lint output (dev-mode):
- "Prompt lint: missing system prompt. Suggest: add \u2018System: You are a helpful assistant...\u2019"
- "Prompt lint: prompt tokens=12345 (>6000). Recommend: use short_summary = extract_summary(prompt)."

How to integrate (code sketch):
- JS/TS SDK: on client creation, attach a small middleware:
  client.use(presetPromptLint({ thresholdTokens: 6000, failInCI: true }))
  client.on('request', telemetryPreset.send)

- Python: wrap the client call in a helper that calls lint_check(prompt) then telemetry.track(preset_map)

Testing and gating:
- Add a CI step in sample-apps that runs lint_check on all example prompts. Fail the build on critical errors.
- Add a smoke test that asserts telemetry keys exist for a synthetic request.

Common gotchas & heuristics learned in field: (notes to self)
- Users paste long PDFs as a single prompt. Lint should auto-detect likely-paste artifacts (many newlines, base64 markers) and give a copy/paste-friendly suggestion: "Consider uploading as embedding + retrieval".
- Function-calling: lib consumers often forget to include schema; provide a tiny generator that creates a starting schema from a JS object.
- Streaming + stop tokens: streaming clients may hang if stop matches are too short. Warn about 1-2 char stops.

Telemetry sampling and cost control:
- Default sample rate: 1% for public quickstarts, 10% for internal preview.
- If you're in Dedicated or Private mode and need 100% coverage, make it opt-in only and route to project-specific telemetry sinks.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Week 0: experimental preset package, installs in three quickstart repos (js, python, go). Manual testing.
- Week 2: CI lint step added to all sample apps; docs page for "prompt lint rules".
- Week 4: telemetry presets enabled in playground and giveaways (sample rate 1%).
- Week 6: gather data on top lint failures and update rules; add an escape hatch for advanced users.

Open questions (needs PM/legal/devexp decisions):
- Should model_hint be a full model id or just family? (Default: family; exposing full id may leak internal mappings.)
- Opt-in strategy for telemetry in enterprise/private: do we default off? (Recommendation: default off in Private.)
- Naming & packaging: single package for both lint + telemetry or two tiny packages? (Prefer two for opt-in flexibility.)

Next immediate tasks (owner: Aisha):
- Create minimal npm/pypi placeholder package scaffolds (stub only) and push to GH (ticketed).
- Add CI lint job to three starter repos.
- Draft the "prompt lint rules" one-pager for internal dev advocates.

Notes / rough TODOs: 
- Add sample-policy snippet for legal indicating what telemetry will and will not capture.
- Build a tiny linter rule for "excessive system prompt personalization" (captures when system prompt contains PII-like tokens).
- Try the heuristics on 50 community examples and collect top 10 failure modes.

References and links: see linked_artifacts above for RFC + GH PR placeholder.

-- End quickstart sketch --

This doc is intentionally terse and action-oriented. Keep iteration cycles short. We want something devs can enable in minutes and that prevents the most common integration pain points.
